query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Stationary friction processing (SFP) improves the oxidation resistance of equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy by refining its grain structure, thereby enhancing the formation of a protective oxide scale.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy in its as-cast state with a coarse grain microstructure (~98 μm) that tends to form nonprotective spinel oxides.
generation.intervention: Application of stationary friction processing using a WC-cylindrical tool at rotational speeds of 400 and 1800 rpm for 5 minutes.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at temperatures of 850 °C, 950 °C, and 1050 °C for 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: An ultrafine-grain microstructure (grain sizes reduced to approximately 1 μm for SFP_400 and 0.43 μm for SFP_1800) with an increased density of grain boundaries and elevated surface free energy.
generation.mechanism: The ultrafine grains and high grain boundary density facilitate rapid outward diffusion of Cr and inward diffusion of oxygen, leading to preferential formation of protective Cr₂O₃ and Al-rich inner oxides. This suppresses the formation of nonprotective spinel phases observed in as-cast samples.
generation.predicted_outcome: SFP-treated samples will display slower oxidation kinetics (evidenced by reduced cumulative mass gain and lower parabolic rate constants) compared to as-cast samples, indicating enhanced oxidation resistance.
generation.baseline: As-cast alloy with coarse grains (~98 μm) that forms nonprotective spinel oxides and exhibits higher oxidation rates.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the specific alloy composition, processing parameters (rotational speeds of 400 and 1800 rpm for 5 minutes), and oxidation conditions (850–1050 °C for 100 hours). Effects outside these parameters are uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: While the observed improvements in oxidation resistance under the given test conditions are clear, uncertainties remain regarding the long-term stability of the protective oxide scale and the scalability of the SFP process to different conditions or alloy systems.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equimolar AlCoCrFeNi samples: one set in the as-cast state and one set processed via stationary friction processing at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes. Expose both sets to isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 hours. Perform comparative analyses on cumulative mass gain, oxidation kinetics, and oxide scale compositions.
measurements: Phase identification of oxide scales using XRD and SEM-EDS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SFP-processed samples do not show significantly lower mass gains, reduced oxidation kinetics, and the formation of predominantly protective oxides (Cr₂O₃ and Al-rich inner oxides) relative to the as-cast samples, then the hypothesis that the ultrafine-grain microstructure produced by SFP enhances oxidation resistance will be rejected.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h.
